description.value: Students design and develop an AI-assisted website prototype for a regional event, club or community organisation. They identify a target audience, create user stories and design criteria, and investigate the information and features users require. Students communicate their proposed solution through a user journey map, site map, alternative interface concepts, annotated wireframes and a visual style guide. They then use generative AI within GitHub Codespaces to produce a functional prototype based on their own design specifications. Students conduct usability testing, compare the prototype against the original user stories and design criteria, and direct AI-assisted improvements to the layout, navigation, accessibility and content. The final submission includes the design portfolio, working prototype, testing evidence, a record of significant AI interactions and an evaluation of the solution and design process.

•	WCAG 2.1 accessibility checklist and design evaluation rubrics
•	Usability testing observation templates and feedback logs

context.value: Regional events, clubs and community organisations rely on websites to share information, attract participants and help people find schedules, locations and registration details. Effective digital design is important because clear navigation, accessible content and thoughtful visual choices make services easier to use. Generative AI supports production, while human decisions remain central to understanding users, testing ideas and improving the final experience.

toComplete.value:
Internal moderation is conducted systematically across the 7–8 band to ensure consistency of teacher judgement against the Australian Curriculum achievement standards. This process involves:

*   **Moderation Conferencing:** Scheduled meetings for the Digital Technologies faculty to review student work samples, specifically focusing on the alignment of the user journey maps and wireframe annotations to the defined design criteria.
*   **Cross-marking:** Departmental validation of the ‘AI Interaction Log’ and final prototype usability results to ensure objective and consistent application of the marking criteria regarding the ethical and effective use of AI tools.
